subject: Vocabulary
topic: Synonyms — SSC CGL Level Word Pairs (W10)

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: BRAVE
questions.explanation: B is correct. BRAVE = ready to face danger or pain without fear; COURAGEOUS is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Reckless' implies bravery without care for consequences — close but not the same (recklessness is foolhardiness, not courage); 'Timid' and 'Fearful' are antonyms.

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: EXQUISITE
questions.explanation: C is correct. EXQUISITE = extremely beautiful, delicate, or fine in quality. SUPERB (of the highest quality) is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Ordinary' and 'Plain' describe something unremarkable — the opposite of exquisite; 'Crude' means rough or unrefined, which is antonymous to exquisite's refinement.

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: ENIGMATIC
questions.explanation: C is correct. ENIGMATIC = difficult to understand or explain; full of mystery. MYSTERIOUS is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Clear' and 'Obvious' are antonyms; 'Simple' contradicts the complexity implied by enigmatic.

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: PROLIFIC
questions.explanation: B is correct. PROLIFIC = producing many works, results, or offspring in a short time. PRODUCTIVE is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Sparse', 'Meagre', and 'Scarce' are antonyms of prolific (they all suggest small quantity). SSC tests prolific in contexts like 'a prolific author' = one who writes many books.

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: AMELIORATE
questions.explanation: C is correct. AMELIORATE = to make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve. IMPROVE is the direct synonym. Trap: 'Worsen' and 'Deteriorate' are antonyms; 'Ignore' implies inaction while ameliorate implies positive action. Root: Latin 'melior' = better (compare: meliorate, ameliorate).

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: ACRIMONY
questions.explanation: B is correct. ACRIMONY = bitterness or ill feeling, especially in speech or manner. BITTERNESS is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Sweetness', 'Kindness', and 'Pleasantness' are all antonyms of acrimony. Example SSC usage: 'The acrimony between the two leaders poisoned the negotiations.'

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: PERFIDIOUS
questions.explanation: B is correct. PERFIDIOUS = guilty of treachery or betrayal; deceitful and untrustworthy. TREACHEROUS is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Loyal', 'Faithful', and 'Trustworthy' are antonyms of perfidious. Root: Latin 'perfidia' = faithlessness (per = through + fides = faith — breaking faith).

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: PUSILLANIMOUS
questions.explanation: C is correct. PUSILLANIMOUS = showing a lack of courage or determination; timid, cowardly. COWARDLY is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Brave', 'Strong', and 'Reckless' all describe the opposite qualities. Root: Latin 'pusillus' (very small) + 'animus' (spirit) — literally 'small-spirited.'

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: SANGUINE
questions.explanation: C is correct. SANGUINE = optimistic, especially in a difficult situation; expecting the best possible outcome. OPTIMISTIC is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Pessimistic', 'Depressed', and 'Anxious' all carry negative outlooks, opposite to sanguine. Note: 'sanguine' also literally means 'blood-red' in heraldry — a common SSC distractor pointing to colour meanings.

questions.stem: Choose the word most SIMILAR in meaning to: INCORRIGIBLE
questions.explanation: D is correct. INCORRIGIBLE = (of a person or behaviour) not able to be corrected, improved, or reformed. IRREDEEMABLE is the closest synonym. Trap: 'Correctable', 'Reformable', and 'Manageable' are all antonyms — they imply the problem can be fixed. Usage: 'an incorrigible liar' = someone who will never stop lying regardless of correction.
